rules.title: Links -lrt
rules.remedy: Drop -lrt on QNX (conditional on the platform), or detect with check_library_exists / AC_SEARCH_LIBS so a missing library is not fatal.
rules.verify: Verified on SDP 8.0 build 141: ld cannot find -lrt.
rules.message: There is no librt in the QNX 8.0 SDP: linking with -lrt fails ('cannot find -lrt', SDP 8.0 build 141, x86_64 and aarch64le). The POSIX realtime functions live in libc.

rules.title: Links Linux/glibc helper libraries (-lnsl -lresolv -lanl -lutil)
rules.remedy: Remove these, or detect per platform. Networking on QNX needs -lsocket (add it explicitly when linking socket code: accept4, getaddrinfo, sendmsg, getifaddrs and others do not link without it in SDP 8.0 build 141). crypt() is declared in <login.h> but no library exports it.
rules.verify: Verified on SDP 8.0 build 141.
rules.message: libnsl, libutil, libresolv, libcrypt and libanl do not exist in the QNX 8.0 SDP (-lX fails with 'cannot find', SDP 8.0 build 141). Socket code needs -lsocket instead (libsocket exists and links).

rules.title: Sanitizer flags
rules.remedy: Keep sanitizer builds as host-only (Linux) test configurations, or use -fsanitize=undefined where supported.
rules.verify: Flag results from qcc link probes on SDP 8.0 build 141.
rules.message: Sanitizers on SDP 8.0 build 141: -fsanitize=undefined and =leak link; =address and =thread are rejected by qcc (libasan exists in the SDP lib dir but the driver rejects the flag in this probe).

rules.title: CMake logic keyed on Linux
rules.remedy: Add a QNX branch (if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "QNX")), or generalise to if(UNIX) where the logic is POSIX-generic. In a toolchain file set CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME to QNX, not Linux.
refs: CMake docs: CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME (QNX is a documented value)
rules.message: A branch or setting assumes Linux. CMake identifies a QNX target as CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME 'QNX'.

rules.title: Socket code without -lsocket
rules.remedy: Add -lsocket to the link line on QNX (LDLIBS += -lsocket; in CMake target_link_libraries(<t> socket) under if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "QNX"); in autoconf AC_SEARCH_LIBS([socket], [socket])). It is harmless to link when the symbols are already in libc.
rules.verify: Verified on SDP 8.0 build 141: link without -lsocket gives 'undefined reference to socket'; with -lsocket it links. Not run on a target.
rules.message: The code calls socket APIs but no build file links -lsocket. On QNX 8.0 the socket functions are not in libc: with the default libraries socket(), bind(), listen(), accept(), connect(), getaddrinfo(), sendmsg(), getifaddrs() and others fail at link time with 'undefined reference' (SDP 8.0 build 141, measured with qcc on x86_64 and aarch64le). libsocket exists and fixes it.

rules.title: Includes a Linux kernel header
rules.remedy: Replace each use with the POSIX/QNX equivalent of what the header supplied (types, constants). If it is a device ioctl header, the device needs a QNX resource-manager interface (devctl) instead.
rules.verify: Checked on SDP 8.0 build 141: no linux/ or asm/ include directory exists. Other SDP versions: verify against SDP.
rules.message: <linux/...> and <asm/...> are Linux kernel uapi headers. The QNX SDP 8.0 (build 141) ships no linux/, asm/ or asm-generic/ directory: every such include fails to compile (checked for 21 common ones with qcc on x86_64 and aarch64le). Many uses are trivial (linux/limits.h, linux/types.h can be replaced by POSIX headers); device-ioctl headers are not.

rules.title: Includes a Linux-specific <sys/...> header
rules.remedy: Remove the include together with the calls it supports (see the per-API findings), or guard it with #if defined(__linux__) and add a __QNXNTO__ branch.
rules.verify: Per-header result from SDP 8.0 build 141 (qcc include probe). Other SDP versions: verify against SDP.
rules.message: This glibc/Linux <sys/...> header is not in the QNX 8.0 SDP for most of the names this rule matches (sys/epoll.h, eventfd.h, signalfd.h, timerfd.h, prctl.h, sendfile.h, sysinfo.h, fanotify.h do not exist in build 141). Two exceptions are present: <sys/inotify.h> (needs -lfsnotify) and <sys/auxv.h> (exists, but getauxval is not declared).

rules.title: epoll event loop
rules.remedy: Port the loop to poll(), ppoll() or select()/pselect() (all four exist in SDP 8.0). ionotify() with SIGEV_PULSE is native QNX (present in the SDP) but only works for resource managers that implement the notify handler for that fd; do not assume it covers sockets. For a pure resource-manager design use the dispatch_* framework (present).
rules.verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141 (header probe, symbol probe, link probe).
rules.message: epoll does not exist on QNX 8.0: no <sys/epoll.h>, no epoll_* symbol in any SDP library, no EPOLL* macro (checked on SDP 8.0 build 141, x86_64 and aarch64le). kqueue/kevent are NOT a way out: <sys/event.h> is not shipped to user code (the BSD event headers sit only in the io-sock driver include tree) and no library exports kqueue or kevent.

rules.title: inotify file watching
rules.remedy: Add -lfsnotify to the link line (on QNX only) and test the event masks the code relies on: only the compile and link steps were verified, no program was run on a QNX target, so semantic parity with Linux inotify (recursive watches, rename events, filesystem coverage) is unchecked. Keep a stat() polling fallback until it has run on the target.
rules.verify: Compile/link verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; runtime behaviour not tested.
rules.message: inotify EXISTS on QNX 8.0: <sys/inotify.h> is in the SDP and libfsnotify exports inotify_init/init1/add_watch/rm_watch (SDP 8.0 build 141: compile and link succeed with -lfsnotify). The IN_* masks (including IN_ACCESS, IN_ATTRIB, IN_CLOSE_WRITE, IN_CREATE, IN_DELETE, IN_MODIFY, IN_MOVED_FROM/TO) and struct inotify_event are defined.

rules.title: eventfd
rules.remedy: Use a pipe() or socketpair() pair when the consumer needs a pollable fd; use a pulse (MsgSendPulse / SIGEV_PULSE) when the consumer already sits in MsgReceive.
rules.verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.
rules.message: eventfd is a Linux file-descriptor wake-up primitive. It does not exist on QNX 8.0 (no <sys/eventfd.h>, no eventfd symbol, no EFD_* macro in SDP 8.0 build 141).

rules.title: sendfile/splice zero-copy calls
rules.remedy: Fall back to a read()/write() loop (or mmap + write) behind a small helper; add a platform fast path only if profiling demands it.
rules.verify: Verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (header, symbol and link probes).
rules.message: Linux zero-copy file transfer calls. On SDP 8.0 build 141: splice, tee, vmsplice, copy_file_range and sendfile64 are not declared. sendfile() is declared in <sys/socket.h> with the BSD signature (7 arguments) but no SDP library exports it: linking fails (also with -lsocket). A same-named Linux call would not have compiled against that prototype anyway.

rules.title: pipe2 / dup3
rules.remedy: pipe2: nothing to change. dup3: use dup2() then fcntl(fd, F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC) (mind the small race window if other threads fork).
rules.verify: Verified on SDP 8.0 build 141: pipe2 present, dup3 absent.
rules.message: On SDP 8.0 build 141 pipe2() is declared in <unistd.h> and exists in libc; dup3() is not declared and no library exports it.

rules.title: prctl
rules.remedy: Map each option individually: PR_SET_NAME -> pthread_setname_np() (declared and exported in SDP 8.0 build 141; so is pthread_getname_np); PR_SET_PDEATHSIG -> a parent-liveness check; PR_SET_DUMPABLE/NO_NEW_PRIVS -> drop (no QNX analogue is known).
rules.verify: Absence and pthread_setname_np verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (probes); argument limits of pthread_setname_np not checked.
rules.message: prctl is a Linux process-control multiplexer. It does not exist on QNX 8.0 (no <sys/prctl.h>, no prctl symbol, no PR_* macro in SDP 8.0 build 141).

rules.title: CPU affinity (sched_setaffinity & friends)
rules.remedy: Use ThreadCtl(_NTO_TCTL_RUNMASK, &mask) for the calling thread (ThreadCtl and _NTO_TCTL_RUNMASK are present in SDP 8.0 build 141; the argument layout and the privilege needed were not tested). Semantics are narrower: Linux sched_setaffinity(pid, ...) can target another process or thread, the runmask call applies to the calling thread, so per-pid callers need restructuring.
rules.verify: Absence verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; ThreadCtl usage not run.
rules.message: Linux affinity API. On SDP 8.0 build 141 sched_setaffinity, sched_getaffinity, pthread_setaffinity_np, pthread_getaffinity_np, pthread_attr_setaffinity_np, cpu_set_t and the CPU_* macros are all missing (the CPU_* set macros exist only in the io-sock driver headers).

rules.title: Raw Linux syscall()
rules.remedy: Replace each call with the libc/POSIX function it wraps. gettid(): include <sys/process.h> and call gettid() (present; whether the number is a Linux-style kernel tid was not checked: use it as a numeric id for logging, not for kernel interfaces). Do not substitute pthread_self() (opaque handle). futex has no mechanical replacement (not declared; no library exports it): redesign onto pthread mutex/condvar.
rules.verify: Verified on SDP 8.0 build 141: syscall and futex absent, gettid present.
rules.message: Linux syscall numbers (SYS_*, __NR_*) have no meaning on QNX, and syscall() is not declared in the SDP (build 141). gettid() DOES exist natively (declared in <sys/process.h>, exported by libc), so SYS_gettid callers need only the call.

rules.title: clone/unshare/setns namespaces
rules.remedy: Use fork()/posix_spawn() and pthreads. Isolation features must be redesigned with QNX process management (no namespace equivalent is assumed).
rules.verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.
rules.message: Linux process/namespace primitives. On SDP 8.0 build 141 clone, unshare, setns and the CLONE_* flags are not available to user code; there is no namespace equivalent.

rules.title: Linux-specific socket options
rules.remedy: Guard each setsockopt/getsockopt with #ifdef so it compiles away when the macro is undefined. Where the macro IS defined (TCP_INFO, TCP_FASTOPEN, SO_REUSEPORT) the struct layout and semantics are BSD's and were not tested: confirm before relying on a same-named constant.
rules.verify: Macro presence verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (compile probe); semantics not run.
rules.message: Socket options that originated on Linux. On SDP 8.0 build 141: TCP_FASTOPEN, TCP_INFO, TCP_NODELAY, TCP_KEEPIDLE/INTVL/CNT, SO_REUSEPORT are defined; TCP_CORK, TCP_QUICKACK, TCP_DEFER_ACCEPT, TCP_USER_TIMEOUT, MSG_MORE, SO_BINDTODEVICE, SO_PRIORITY, SO_MARK, IP_PKTINFO-style Linux options are not.

rules.title: Linux-only open() flags
rules.remedy: Drop or emulate: O_TMPFILE -> mkstemp()+unlink(); O_PATH -> open(O_RDONLY) is not equivalent (symlink handling and permission checks differ), so check what the caller needs; O_NOATIME -> omit; O_DIRECT -> omit (the SDP defines no such flag).
rules.verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.
rules.message: These open() flags originated on Linux. None of O_PATH, O_TMPFILE, O_NOATIME, O_DIRECT is defined in SDP 8.0 build 141.

rules.title: sysinfo()
rules.remedy: Use sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE) and sysconf(_SC_PHYS_PAGES)/_SC_AVPHYS_PAGES (all three names are defined in SDP 8.0 build 141; what values they return on a target was not tested); uptime from clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC); the QNX system page (<sys/syspage.h>, SYSPAGE_ENTRY and asinfo) is the usual source for memory facts, so check there as well.
rules.verify: Absence and macro names verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; return values not run.
rules.message: Linux sysinfo structure/call (memory, uptime, load). Neither the call nor struct sysinfo exists in SDP 8.0 build 141 (no <sys/sysinfo.h>).

rules.title: mremap / Linux mmap flags
rules.remedy: Replace mremap by mmap new + copy/munmap old (or reserve address space up front); drop MAP_POPULATE/HUGETLB hints.
rules.verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.
rules.message: mremap and these mmap flags are Linux-specific. mremap, MAP_POPULATE, MAP_HUGETLB and MAP_GROWSDOWN do not exist in SDP 8.0 build 141.

rules.title: Linux/glibc non-portable pthread calls
rules.remedy: pthread_yield -> sched_yield(); tryjoin/timedjoin -> a completion flag + condition variable with timed wait.
rules.verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.
rules.message: glibc _np extensions. On SDP 8.0 build 141 pthread_getattr_np, pthread_tryjoin_np, pthread_timedjoin_np and pthread_yield do not exist (pthread_setname_np and pthread_getname_np do, and are not matched by this rule).

rules.title: Linux-only clock ids
rules.remedy: Use CLOCK_MONOTONIC / CLOCK_REALTIME; keep the Linux ids behind #ifdef CLOCK_BOOTTIME.
rules.verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.
rules.message: Clock ids that are Linux extensions. CLOCK_BOOTTIME, CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, CLOCK_*_COARSE, CLOCK_TAI and the *_ALARM ids are not defined in SDP 8.0 build 141; CLOCK_MONOTONIC and CLOCK_REALTIME are.

rules.title: System V IPC
rules.remedy: POSIX shm_open()/sem_open()/mq_open() for a quick port; for a request/reply design use native message passing (ChannelCreate/ConnectAttach, MsgSend/MsgReceive/MsgReply).

rules.message: The Linux /proc/<pid>/exe symlink is not a QNX interface.

rules.title: Linux /proc paths
rules.remedy: Replace with POSIX/QNX queries: sysconf(), getrusage(), the system page (<sys/syspage.h>) for CPU/memory facts, procfs ioctls (DCMD_PROC_*) for process info.
rules.verify: verify against SDP: procfs layout on QNX 8.0.
rules.message: QNX has a /proc, but it is a different interface (process address spaces, not Linux text files).

rules.title: Linux /sys (sysfs) paths
rules.remedy: Query the real source: sysconf/getifaddrs for system facts, device resource managers for hardware state, the system page for CPU data.
rules.verify: verify against SDP.
rules.message: sysfs is a Linux kernel pseudo-filesystem; not assumed on QNX.
